Relax the Actionable Bounds That Estimates Are at

Source: R/mxHelper-relax-bounds-at-bounds.R
MxHelperRelaxBoundsAtBounds.Rd

Moves each finite bound that an estimate is at, when the hit is actionable (MxHelperAtBounds()), away from zero by factor: a negative bound is multiplied by it, a positive one divided. With protect_lb_zero = TRUE, a lower bound of zero is kept. When the new bounds of a parameter cross, they are set around their midpoint. Stops with an error unless factor > 1. The arguments are checked first; the internal version, without checks, is the one other projects copy.

Usage

MxHelperRelaxBoundsAtBounds(
  x,
  factor = 10,
  abs_bnd_tol = 1e-06,
  rel_bnd_tol = 1e-04,
  exclude = NULL,
  protect_lb_zero = TRUE,
  allowed_bounds = NULL
)

Arguments

x

An OpenMx model (MxModel), usually fitted.

factor

Number greater than 1. Factor by which a bound is moved away from zero.

abs_bnd_tol

Positive number. Absolute tolerance for an estimate at a bound.

rel_bnd_tol

Positive number. Tolerance for an estimate at a bound, relative to the larger of the absolute estimate, the absolute bound, and 1.

exclude

Character vector or NULL. Labels of parameters whose bounds are never relaxed.

protect_lb_zero

Logical. If TRUE, a lower bound of zero is never relaxed.

allowed_bounds

List or NULL. Parameters allowed to rest at a bound: a list with the character vectors lower and upper of parameter labels. Their bound hits are reported but are not actionable.

Value

Returns the model with the new bounds.

See also

Other Bounds Functions: MxHelperAtBounds(), MxHelperNudgeOffBounds(), MxHelperRelaxBounds()

Author

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Examples

set.seed(seed = 42)
x <- data.frame(
  y1 = rnorm(n = 50),
  y2 = rnorm(n = 50)
)
fit <- MxHelperQuiet(
  expr = MxHelperMuSigma(
    x = x,
    extraTries = 2
  )
)
fit <- MxHelperRelaxBoundsAtBounds(
  x = fit
)
